key_insight: Self-supervised JEPA learns XRD representations that support crystal-property prediction and reveal continuous structure in peak broadening and multi-phase mixtures.
engineering_relevance: Reusable XRD embeddings could support automated diffraction analysis for high-throughput materials discovery without requiring explicit supervision for every phase combination.
method: Learn representations from 1D diffraction patterns using masked prediction in latent space.
Train lightweight attentive probes on frozen embeddings for space group classification and lattice parameter estimation.
Probe latent trajectories for peak broadening and decode paths between single-phase representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports probe accuracy close to much larger supervised vision transformers, smooth latent trajectories for peak broadening, and realistic decoded multi-phase patterns without explicit multi-phase supervision.
watch_item: Realistic decoded mixtures do not establish reliable phase identification or quantification on experimental multi-phase XRD data.
paper_title: Exploring Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures for Self-Supervised Representation Learning of Powder X-ray Diffraction Patterns
